skills.name: Sequence of tenses and reported viewpoints

note.text: Under a past reporting frame, backshift often changes present to past and present perfect to past perfect; will may become would. Pronouns and words such as tomorrow can also change when the reporting viewpoint changes. A form should preserve who did what and when. Backshift is not compulsory in every report: information still true or relevant can remain in a present form. Past perfect normally stays past perfect. Exercises must state the intended frame where several choices could be valid.

sections.heading: Your goal and connections
sections.text: By the end, you should be able to preserve references and relative time when backshift is requested while recognising contexts that retain a tense. Builds on: tense patterns and narrative time. Leads to: conditional meanings and accurate reporting in articles.

sections.heading: Understand the pattern

sections.heading: Read the original model
sections.text: Original model: Bih said, I have written the note. A later report with backshift says she had {participle("write")} the note. Ayuk said he would return the next day when reporting is from a later viewpoint. Compare an ongoing fact reported as still true: the club coordinator says or said that the room is available, if availability remains current in the stated context.

sections.heading: Apply and check
sections.text: Mark the reporting time and the original reference first. Adjust tense, pronouns and relative time only as the intended perspective requires. Check auxiliaries and participles separately; a correct reporting pattern cannot rescue an incorrect verb form.

cards.idea: A correction must preserve the intended meaning and form.
example: Every present form must change in every reported statement. Correction: Still-true information can sometimes retain its tense.
Changing all pronouns at random preserves the message. Correction: The referents must remain clear and consistent.
Tomorrow names the same calendar day in every utterance. Correction: The day depends on the original and reporting situations.
Past perfect always shifts into will have in past reporting. Correction: That would change the time relation instead of preserving it.

pick.q: The exercise asks for past reporting with backshift: Bih said, “I am ready.” Choose the matching report.
pick.r: Bih said that she was ready.
w: Bih said that I am ready, with Bih still the referent of I.
Bih said that she were ready.
Bih said that she will ready.
e: The report changes the speaker reference and the task explicitly asks for backshift.
The ordinary singular reported statement uses was.
Will ready lacks the required be and changes the target.
pick.y: Keep reference and the requested reporting perspective.

pick.q: Backshift the completed statement under a past reporting frame: Ayuk said, “I have written the note.”
pick.r: Ayuk said that he had written the note.
w: Ayuk said that he had wrote the note.
Ayuk said that he has writing the note.
Ayuk said that she had written the note, with she still referring to Ayuk.
e: Had takes the participle written.
The perfect needs a participle, not this -ing form.
The pronoun does not preserve the stated reference.
pick.y: Use had plus participle and preserve the speaker.

pick.q: A speaker said yesterday, “I will return tomorrow.” Report it later, from a different day, with ordinary backshift.
pick.r: The speaker said they would return the next day.
w: The speaker said they would returned the next day.
The speaker said they will returning yesterday.
The speaker said tomorrow must keep exactly the same date in every report.
e: Would takes the base return.
The verb group and time reference are inconsistent.
The relative time word depends on the reporting viewpoint.
pick.y: Both modal and time expression follow the changed frame.

pick.q: Which claim about sequence of tenses is accurate?
pick.r: Backshift can be unnecessary when the reported information is still true or relevant.
w: Every report must shift every verb regardless of context.
Past perfect must always shift to a new invented tense.
A reporting verb makes all pronouns meaningless.
e: Context can support retaining a present form.
Past perfect normally stays unchanged in the taught model.
References still need to be preserved.
pick.y: Do not turn a useful reporting pattern into an absolute rule.
